verdict: KEEP as proved Gaussian special case; DROP any implication that it establishes P0321
exact_statement: For the stipulated cutoff Gaussian displacement field with transverse covariance aT|k|^-2 PT and longitudinal covariance aL|k|^-s PL (aT>0,aL>=0,0<=s<2), its density-wave surrogate decays as a positive constant times r^-aT|q|²/(4π), and its linearized sixfold orientation surrogate has a positive limiting correlation.
assumptions: Cutoff Lambda>0, q≠0, stationary increments, fixed direction, the orientation observable is curl(u)/2; no Riesz particle identification.
proof_or_counterexample: Independently: angular integration gives π[1-J0(t)-cos(2α)J2(t)] and the radial integral is log r+O(1), so Var(q·Δu)=aT|q|² log r/(2π)+O(1). The curl spectrum is aT/4 on the cutoff disk, hence Var θ=aT Λ²/(16π) and Gaussian characteristic functions yield lim C6=exp(-36 Var θ)>0.
remaining_gap: Transfer from Gaussian elastic field to Gibbs particle process and Delaunay orientational observable, plus defect proliferation yielding fast translational decay. This surrogate itself has algebraic translational decay, so it is not a hexatic phase.

exact_statement: An exponential moment at q, logarithmic variance κ2=a log r+O(1), and uniformly absolutely summable higher cumulants at q imply two-sided bounds |E exp(iqX)|=exp(O(1))r^-q²a/2.
assumptions: E exp(q|X|)<∞; a,q>0; uniform D,B; cumulants are Taylor coefficients of log mgf near 0.
proof_or_counterexample: Reproduced: absolute cumulant convergence makes K(z) analytic in |z|<q and continuous at iq; M(z)=exp K(z) near 0 extends by identity theorem through the disk; dominated convergence takes z=itq to iq; Re K(iq)=-q²κ2/2+O(B). No scale independence is used.
remaining_gap: No cumulant hypotheses verified for a microscopic Riesz Gibbs state or sixfold bond angle.

exact_statement: Anchored absolute joint-cumulant bounds with summable scale weights imply the higher-cumulant bound in L1 without independent increments.
assumptions: Finite joint exponential moment; for each n≥3 and anchor j, sum over remaining indices of |cum|≤n!b_n y_j; sum_j y_j≤Y; sum_n q^n b_n<∞.
proof_or_counterexample: By multilinearity κ_n(sum_j Z_j)=sum_{j1,...,jn} cum(Z_j1,...,Z_jn); anchoring j1 and summing absolute values yields |κ_n|≤n!b_nY, then sum with q^n/n!.
remaining_gap: The anchored bound and separate variance estimate are unproved for jellium defects.

exact_statement: If the physical bond correlation equals a nonzero bounded amplitude times the L1 vertex correlation plus O(r^-η-δ) uniformly in volume, its magnitude is two-sided Θ(r^-η) at large r.
assumptions: Amplitude magnitude in [A_-,A_+], A_->0; δ>0 and uniform E0; L1; thermodynamic limit only if separately established.
proof_or_counterexample: Triangle and reverse-triangle inequalities give lower A_-e^-H r^-η-E0r^-η-δ and upper A_+e^H r^-η+E0r^-η-δ; at r^δ≥2E0e^H/A_- the lower is at least half its leading term.
remaining_gap: The representation, nonzero amplitude and subleading error for the actual bond observable are precisely unproved; positional disorder is separate.

verdict: KEEP as a counterexample to variance-only inference
exact_statement: At r=2^J the sum of J independent fair signs scaled by π/(2q) has variance proportional to log r while its q-characteristic function is zero for every J≥1.
assumptions: q>0; independent fair signs only for the constructed example.
proof_or_counterexample: Variance=(π/(2q))²J; factorization gives E e^{iqX}=cos(π/2)^J=0. Therefore logarithmic variance does not imply an algebraic vertex lower bound.
remaining_gap: This tests a proof inference only; it is not a Riesz Gibbs construction.

verdict: KEEP as a sharp-scale pair-law counterexample
exact_statement: For a=r^-η≤1/4, the wrapped Gaussian first Fourier coefficient a can be erased by a positive circular density at total-variation distance 2a/π.
assumptions: η>0; a≤1/4; pair laws need not form a consistent stationary process.
proof_or_counterexample: Subtract (a/π)cosφ from wrapped-Gaussian density. The remaining higher-harmonic density is positive because 2∑_{n≥2}a^{n²}≤2a⁴/(1-a²)<1. Its first Fourier coefficient is 0. With TV=sup_A|P(A)-Q(A)|, half the L¹ distance is (a/(2π))∫|cosφ|dφ=2a/π.
remaining_gap: Shows transfer error must be below leading correlation scale; does not verify any Riesz approximation.
